assumptions: Frame: Earth-centred inertial fixed at liftoff, z along the spin axis, x through the launch meridian at liftoff; no epoch, so the orbit's node in J2000 is not fixed here (module 37). Time: seconds from liftoff (holddown release).

Earth: a sphere of radius 6378136.6 m (Aster pck00010 a), point-mass gravity GM 398600441800000 m^3/s^2 (Aster delta-v.ts), rotating at 0.00007292115373194001 rad/s (pck00010); no J2, no oblate surface.
Atmosphere: the 1976 US Standard (idea 02's isa(), PartForge), no wind; above 85999.95 m (the top of its table) density and pressure taken as zero.

Drag: q S C_A(M), S from a 4 m diameter, C_A the Apollo/Saturn V wind-tunnel forebody coefficient digitized from Walker, NASA TM X-53770, Figure 28, held flat outside Mach 0.5 to 7.8; applied to this vehicle as a shape it may not have; no lift, no normal force at angle of attack.

Thrust: n [F_vac(tau) - p_a A_e] from idea 33 via idea 34; at throttle tau the engine flow scales with idea 33's chamber flow (gas-generator flow proportional, assumed); no thrust build-up or tail-off impulse; no engine cant.

Steering in a launch plane fixed in inertial space at liftoff (no yaw steering): vertical, a pitch kick held until the Earth-relative velocity turns as far, then zero angle of attack (gravity turn); upper stages pitch from 9.15 to 0 deg above the horizon, linear in time. Open loop: no guidance (module 36).

assumptions: Frames: geometry and the coast in the mean equator and equinox of date (IAU 2006 bias-precession, ERFA's coefficients); everything handed on in J2000 (ICRF axes, Aster's frame). Idea 36's frame (x through the launch meridian at liftoff) is that frame turned by the pad's right ascension at liftoff.

Time: UTC from the clock, TT = UTC + (TAI - UTC from NAIF naif0012.tls) + 32.184 s; TDB = TT (periodic terms under 2 ms ignored, as Aster does); UT1 = UTC (|UT1 - UTC| < 0.9 s, not modelled). Nutation is not modelled (Earth's pole and sidereal time are the mean ones).

Launch site: latitude 28.5 deg on Aster's sphere (the latitude idea 35 flew from), east longitude -80.60542 deg (Pad 39A placed from MPR-SAT-FE-73-1 Table 4-3 (S-IC/S-II separation 94.7 km down range on the 91.504 deg flight azimuth, at 28.580 N, -79.637 E), walked back on a sphere of Aster's radius).

The parking orbit's plane passes through the pad at liftoff (no dogleg) and, after the coast, contains the asymptote. Coast: point-mass gravity (Aster's GM) plus J2 (WGS-84, NAIF geophysical.ker), RK4 at 10 s; no drag, no J3 or higher, no Sun or Moon, no venting.
The departure point is where an impulsive burn at the hyperbola's perigee leaves along the asymptote (JPL 82-43 eq. 21-22 with theta_2 = nu_I = 0); module 38 replaces it with a finite burn.
The asymptote is held fixed for the day (JPL 82-43: "may be considered constant for a given day of launch").

refusals.reason: No start or cutoff transient and no venting: the engine runs at its deck's vacuum thrust from ignition to cutoff, and nothing boils off in the coast. On Apollo 17 the start and cutoff transients gave 811.8 and 205.8 kN s, and the S-IVB vented 1041 kg of hydrogen in its 3 h coast (MPR-SAT-FE-73-1 sections 7.6, 7.8, Table 16-9).
refusals.what_would_help: Transient and venting models for this engine and stage.

refusals.reason: The asymptote handed on has J2 followed out to 20 Earth radii but not the Moon or the Sun: their pull on the way out of the Earth's sphere of influence is not in it.
refusals.what_would_help: A propagation with the Moon and the Sun out of the Earth's sphere of influence (module 40).

assumptions: The burn is flown in idea 37's frame (mean equator and equinox of date at liftoff, J2 about its z axis) and every state handed on is turned back to J2000 (ICRF axes) with idea 37's precession; epochs in TDB seconds past J2000 beside UTC.
Gravity: point mass (Aster's GM) plus J2 (WGS-84), as idea 37's coast; no drag, no Sun or Moon, no venting during the coast or the burn.

Engine: constant vacuum thrust and flow (no start or cutoff transient, no throttling, no mixture-ratio shift) unless replaying Apollo 17; thrust scale multiplies thrust and flow together, exhaust velocity unchanged.

Cutoff: when the energy conserved under point mass + J2 reaches C3/2 (so the C3 is reached at infinity in this gravity model; the two-body C3 at cutoff, idea 37's and Aster's convention, is handed beside it); the asymptote is the hyperbola's after the coast is followed with J2 to 20 Earth radii, targeted onto idea 37's by the ignition time and a constant yaw.
Steering tangential, one burn; the plane is the parking orbit's (no yaw).

refusals.reason: 27 Delta-DOR baseline sessions found no hour with both stations above 10 deg: the spacecraft's declination puts it out of their common sky.
refusals.what_would_help: Another agency's antennas for a north-south baseline (ESA, as Lucy's paper notes), or fewer sessions.

assumptions: Frame: heliocentric ICRF/J2000 axes, Sun centre (as idea 39 and Aster); time TDB seconds past J2000, UTC = TDB - 69.184 s, UT1 = UTC.

Forces: the Sun (GM 132712440018000000000, Aster), the Earth (GM 398600441800000, Aster; J2 0.00108262539 about the ICRF z axis, DE440), the Moon and Mercury..Neptune system barycentres (DE440 GMs), the Sun's Schwarzschild term (c 299792458 m/s); planets by Chebyshev fits of JPL Horizons (Aster's daily file and fetched records); no asteroid perturbers, no non-gravitational forces on the target.
Integrator: Dormand-Prince 5(4), relative tolerance 1e-12; the state transition matrix integrated from the point-mass gravity gradient (J2, relativity and sunlight left out of it).

Navigation: linear covariance analysis; Doppler every 2 h of a pass, one range point per pass, Delta-DOR on two baselines; stations turned by the Earth rotation angle only; light time ignored; data cut off 3 days before each TCM.
TCMs: impulsive, fixed-time position targeting of the arrival; statistics from 4000 seeded samples of N(deterministic, G P G^T); execution errors by Gates' model.
